title: TCP/IP fundamentals and network topology flaws
goal_html: Students trace a network connection through all four TCP/IP layers, identify which header fields are forgeable, and explain why a flat network topology amplifies risk. Ties to LO 3.1.A (describe TCP/IP stack structure and topology-based attack surfaces).
steps_html:
1. Each pair opens the simulation and steps through the simulated TCP connection. For each packet displayed, they label: (a) which layer's header is shown, (b) which field could be forged by an attacker and why.
  2. Pairs draw a simple network diagram showing two scenarios: a flat network and a segmented network. For each, they mark where a compromised host could reach without crossing a firewall.
  3. Using the packet log in the simulation, pairs identify which packets show evidence of IP spoofing and write one sentence describing the defense that would block each one.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: one partner is the "network analyst" (describes what each header field means legitimately), the other is the "attacker" (explains how to forge or abuse that field). Swap roles halfway through. For the topology diagram step, both partners must agree before writing.
exit_html: Each student submits: the name of the TCP/IP layer targeted by IP spoofing, the name of one network topology defense, and one sentence explaining why switches alone do not prevent all sniffing attacks.
